lead: Primary PPH is blood loss ≥ 500 mL after vaginal birth or ≥ 1000 mL at caesarean within 24 h, or any loss that makes her unstable. It is a leading cause of maternal death; uterine atony causes most cases.
f: Primary: within 24 h · Secondary: abnormal bleeding from 24 h to 12 wk · Minor 500–1000 mL, stable · Major over 1000 mL or shock · Placental bed takes 500–800 mL/min; crossing fibres act as living ligatures

tr: Loss is underestimated (clot in a soft uterus); tachycardia comes first, low BP means ≥ 30% of volume is lost

f: Tone (about 70%): overdistension (twins, polyhydramnios, macrosomia), grand multipara, fibroids, long or fast labour, chorioamnionitis, MgSO₄, nifedipine, anaemia · Trauma (20%): instrumental birth, precipitate labour, macrosomia, VBAC · Tissue (10%): retained placenta, accreta, succenturiate lobe · Thrombin (under 1%): DIC (abruption, PE, HELLP, IUFD, sepsis, AFE), anticoagulants

sc: Uterus soft, above the umbilicus → Tone: atony
Uterus hard, steady bright bleeding after forceps → Trauma: tear
Twins, 18 h on oxytocin, 900 mL loss → Uterine atony

f: FBC, cross-match 4–6 units, clotting, fibrinogen, RFT, LFT, bedside clot test · Do not wait for results · Complications: shock, DIC, organ failure, death; transfusion reactions; hysterectomy; anaemia, sepsis, Sheehan syndrome

sc: Cannot breastfeed and no periods after a massive PPH → Sheehan syndrome

f: Call for help; all first steps at once · Two cannulae, bloods, warm crystalloid 20 mL/kg, then blood (O-negative if needed) · Tranexamic acid 1 g IV over 10 min within 3 h of birth · Empty the bladder (catheter) · Chart pulse, BP, SpO₂, urine and loss every 15 min

sc: Bleeding 4 h after birth, TXA not given → Too late for TXA

f: Rub up the uterus, then drugs · Oxytocin 10 IU slowly then 40 IU over 4 h: first line; fast bolus drops BP · Ergometrine 0.5 mg IM or slow IV: not in hypertension, PE or heart disease · Misoprostol 800 µg sublingual or rectal: fever, shivering; no fridge · Carboprost 250 µg deep IM every 15 min, max 8 doses: not in asthma

Bimanual compression buys time · Balloon tamponade (Bakri or condom catheter, 300–500 mL saline, 12–24 h) with oxytocin and antibiotics · Laparotomy: repair tears, then B-Lynch suture (works in about 9 of 10) → uterine artery ligation → internal iliac ligation → hysterectomy (decide early if she is getting worse)

sc: Atony after oxytocin, ergometrine and misoprostol → Bimanual compression, then balloon
Atony not controlled, wants more children → B-Lynch suture

f: Retained placenta: not out 30 min after active management (60 min physiological) → manual removal in theatre + antibiotics; will not separate: suspect accreta · Trauma: good light, repair tears; rupture → laparotomy · Inversion: shock out of proportion, no fundus felt: push it back at once, then oxytocin · Thrombin: FFP 4 units per 6 units of red cells, platelets if under 50, cryoprecipitate if fibrinogen under 2 g/L

sc: Shock after cord traction, no fundus felt → Uterine inversion

f: Causes: endometritis, retained products; rarely choriocarcinoma · Clues: pain, bulky uterus, open os, fever, offensive lochia · FBC, cultures, scan, β-hCG if it persists · IV cephalosporin + metronidazole, uterotonics, evacuation if tissue retained

sc: Bleeding weeks later with high β-hCG → Choriocarcinoma

f: Treat anaemia; high-risk women deliver where blood and theatre exist; partograph · Active third stage for every birth: oxytocin 10 IU IM within 1 min (or misoprostol 600 µg oral) · Delayed cord clamping 1–3 min · Controlled cord traction · Check the placenta is complete; uterine tone checks every 15 min for 2 h (WHO) · Watch every mother for the first 4 h
